record.headline: Cognition halved the user cap on the Teams plan from 200 to 100 and reshuffled which features come with it.
record.who: Teams customers with more than 100 users, and teams that relied on priority support or the admin analytics dashboard.
record.read: Teams looks to be pushed toward a mid-size ceiling with larger organisations steered to Enterprise, while SSO moving down makes Teams easier to sell to security-minded buyers.
record.caveat: Before page is the 24 Oct capture. The Enterprise Security list still shows SAML/OIDC SSO, so SSO may now sit on both plans.

rows: NetFlow Monitoring, per million records per month
record.who: NetFlow Monitoring customers on the retention tier shown beside this price.
record.read: A steep unit price cut on a niche network product suggests Datadog is competing for network-flow volume or simplifying retention pricing.
record.caveat: The page lists several retention tiers (15 to 90 days and over 90 days) beside one price, so it is not certain which tier the new price applies to.

record.headline: Render removed the 24-hour session cap on sandboxes and no longer lists 1 GB of included SSD storage on Postgres.
record.who: Sandbox users running long sessions, and Postgres users who counted on the 1 GB included storage line.
record.read: Dropping the session cap makes sandboxes better suited to long-running agent work, while the Postgres storage line may reflect a move to purely metered storage.
record.caveat: The page layout is ambiguous: the 1 GB line may have moved rather than been removed, and an unstable variant of this page was also seen on 8 Nov.
